summary: Added getOrderedActiveStages to the import block in workflow-handoff.ts (was missing from the existing import).

Inserted step 2b loop in getProjectManagerHandoff() between step 2 (READY WPs) and step 3 (all terminal). The loop scans non-terminal, non-dependency-blocked IN_PROGRESS WPs for pending pipeline stages using three guards: FAIL guard (breaks — downstream agent's own handoff handles it), current-stage IN_PROGRESS guard (breaks — stage already being worked on), upstream IN_PROGRESS guard (breaks — premature routing prevention). Routes to PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP[stage] when all guards pass.

Updated the existing R5.10 test in WP-005 describe block — it used zero-pipeline IN_PROGRESS WPs which now correctly route to Developer via step 2b, so updated it to use impl IN_PROGRESS pipelines (which trigger the current-stage guard and still produce WAIT).

Added 11 new test cases in a new 'WP-003: getProjectManagerHandoff — step 2b pipeline routing' describe block covering: impl PASS → READY_FOR_QA, impl+qa PASS → READY_FOR_REVIEW, QA FAIL guard → WAIT, impl IN_PROGRESS guard → WAIT, READY WP priority over step 2b, dep-blocked skip → WAIT, all-stages PASS → WAIT, custom active_pipeline_stages routing, upstream IN_PROGRESS guard, zero-pipeline freshly-claimed WP (default stages → Developer, documentation-only → Documentation, custom [qa,code-review] → QA).
All 1863 tests pass (149 in workflow-handoff.test.ts). Zero regressions.

comments.note: In workflow-handoff.ts, the step 2b loop uses `wp.pipelines.filter(p => p.type === stage && !p.auto_cancelled)` twice (once for the current stage and once for the upstream). This pattern is shared with several other handoff functions in the same file. A small private helper (e.g., `latestNonCancelledPipeline(pipelines, type)`) would eliminate the repetition and make the intent clearer, but extracting it was out of scope for this WP.

The `makeWp` test helper in workflow-handoff.test.ts always sets `assigned_to: 'Developer'`. Tests that need a different assigned_to must spread and override the value. A second overload or an optional parameter for `assigned_to` would make override intent explicit in test call sites, but this is pre-existing debt and low priority.

comments.note: The upstream IN_PROGRESS guard in step 2b (workflow-handoff.ts:397-403) is effectively unreachable in standard pipeline flow. For it to fire, the current stage (e.g., qa) must have zero non-auto-cancelled pipelines while the upstream stage (e.g., impl) is simultaneously IN_PROGRESS — but the inner loop would have already broken on the current-stage IN_PROGRESS guard when processing impl. The guard is harmless defensive code, and test 2b.9 (labeled 'upstream IN_PROGRESS guard') actually exercises the current-stage guard path. All WAIT outcomes are correct regardless.

Test 2b.9 title says 'upstream IN_PROGRESS guard' but the inline comment correctly identifies that the current-stage guard (qa IN_PROGRESS → break) is what fires. Minor documentation inconsistency in test naming — no behavioral impact.
